newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fashion designer Gianni Versace was shot dead in front of his South Beach villa. Suspected killer is a Filipino-American who is also wanted for four other murders. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos rejected calls by leftist group for Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson to resign after the peso plunged following its de facto devaluation. (MANILA STANDARD)
- President Ramos said the country will maintain its economic growth target of seven percent this year despite the peso's fall. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said the peso was stabilising at 29 pesos to 29.50 to the dollar. (MALAYA)
- Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said panic over price hikes is not necessary since prices of food will not shoot up as long as oil prices remain stable. (MANILA TIMES)
- Senate President Ernesto Maceda said the Senate has decided to make its own inquiry starting next week into the sharp drop in the peso's value.
- A senator admitted knowing a Filipino-Chinese businessman suspected to be a drug dealer saying the latter should be given a chance to defend himself in court. (INQUIRER)
- Defense Secretary Renato de Villa said illegal drugs are now the biggest threat to the national security and called on Congress to give more teeth to the Dangerous Drugs Act. (MANILA BULLETIN)
